Heard Sri Deepak Kumar Yadav, learned counsel for the revisionist, learned A.G.A. for the State-respondent, Sri Rajesh Kumar Yadav, learned counsel for the opposite party No.2 and perused the material available on record.

2. The instant Criminal Revision has been preferred by the revisionist for setting aside the impugned judgement and order dated 13.08.2024 passed by Principal Judge, Family Court, District Sambhal situated at Chandausi in Case No.198 of 2021 (Smt. Payal vs. Gaurav Sharma @ Indramohan, under Section 125 Cr.P.C., Police Station Rajpura, District Sambhal, whereby the opposite party No.2 has been awarded Rs.4000/- per month from the date of filing of application on 27.04.2021 to date of judgment and Rs.8,000/- per month from the date of impugned judgment i.e. 13.08.2024.

sentences.text:
Factual matrix of the case is that marriage of the revisionist (Gaurav Sharma) was solemnized with opposite party No.2 (Smt. Payal) according to Hindu rites and rituals on 24.06.2019 and parents of the opposite party No.2 (Smt. Payal) had given sufficient gifts and dowry in the marriage,
but her husband and in-laws were not satisfied with the dowry and thereafter they used to demand a swift car and Rs.2 lac cash when the opposite party No.2 expressed her inability to fulfil their demand, on 21.06.2020, her husband gave her beating, due to which, her child in the womb died and her husband did not provide her medical treatment.
When her father and uncle went to meet her, they were also beaten by revisionist and her in-laws.
In July, 2020, her in-laws left her to the border of her parental village with warning that never come back without fulfilling their demand of dowry.
Thereafter, her father lodged a complaint at the Police Counselling Centre, in which, a date was fixed on 06.03.2021.

There upon on 07.03.2021, her husband, mother-in-law, brother-in-law (dewar), sister-in-law (nanad) visited her house in the morning and pressurized her to enter into compromise and when she refused the same, they gave her beating and repeated their demanded dowry.
When the crowd gathered there, they escaped from the house of the opposite party no.2 after giving threat of life.
In this regard, she lodged an FIR, vide Case Crime No.38 of 2021, under Sections 498A, 323, 504, 506 I.P.C. and Section Dowry Prohibition Act.

Her husband has neglected to maintain her since she was turned out from her matrimonial home and never took her back to his place, whereas opposite party No.2 is legally wedded wife of the revisionist (Gaurav Sharma @
Indramohan) and he has responsibility to maintain her.
She has no independent source of income and her husband works as a cashier in ICICI Bank situated at Sector-18, Noida and earns around Rs.45,000/- per month.

He also possess 10 bigha agricultural land from which, he gets Rs.20,000/-
annual income.
He also earns Rs.30,000/- as rent from house built in 200 square yards as well as Rs.15,000/- also earns from selling milk of cow and buffalo.
Thus, he earns Rs.90,000/- per month from all sources.
The opposite party No.2 is living life of a deserted wife and she claimed Rs.45,000/- per month as maintenance.

4. The trial Court had summoned the revisionist (Gaurav Sharma @ Indramohan), who appeared and filed his written statement, in which, he accepted the factum of marriage between the parties,
but he denied the allegations of torture, physical assault and matrimonial cruelty levelled against him by the opposite party No.2.
He also stated therein that he is still ready to take back the opposite party No.2.

He had filed a suit for restitution of conjugal rights before the family Court, under Section 9 of the Hindu Marriage Act, which was registered as Matrimonial Suit No.41 of 2020, in which, opposite party No.2 appeared and stated that she is still residing at her parental house.
She is a skilled woman and she also helps her parents in agricultural work and animal husbandry.
He is not employed anywhere and he has only 4 bighas agricultural land and earns his livelihood by farming and doing labour work.
He also bears burden of maintaining his old aged mother.
He has not any rented house in the village and he is not engaging any business of selling milk.
The opposite party No.2 has taken away all her streedhan and jewellery.
She used to talk to some unknown person on mobile phone and when he intervened, she had thrown her mobile phone on the ground and it got broken.
She also used to threatened that she implicate him in false case of demand of dowry.
She is a free minded women and seeks to live a free life according to her choice.
5. The trial Court, after considering the pleadings of the parties and appreciating the evidence adduced by them, gave findings that opposite party No.2 is legally wedded wife of revisionist.

She is Gaurav Sharma @ Indramohan vs State Of U.P. And Another on 5 June, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/31309796/
2 residing separately from her husband with sufficient reason as she is the victim of demand of dowry and practices of matrimonial cruelty and harassment by her husband and in-laws.

sentences.text: There is no evidence on record that she is having any independent earnings.
Thus, she is unable to maintain herself.

The opposite party No.2 (P.W.1) has stated, in his evidence, that her husband is cashier in ICICI Bank and he possess agricultural land in his village, but she could not produce any documents in support of her assertion.

P.W.2 (father of the opposite party No.2) has stated, in his evidence, that revisionist (Gaurav Sharma @ Indramohan) works in the Bank of Baroda, Salempur Branch, District Bulandshahar, but he has not produced any evidence in this regard.

The revisionist has admitted that his father died in the year 2007-2008 and he worked in D.T.C. (Delhi Transports Corporation)
and he died during service.
His elder brother is posted in BSF, one brother works in R.P.F. and his younger brother works in military.
He is not posted in ICICI Bank as cashier and he never did any service.
He receives family pension of Rs.9-10 thousand.
His father owned 15 bighas agricultural land from which, he obtained 3 bighas land on his share and he does not cultivate the land.

Therefore, trial Court has awarded Rs.4,000/- as maintenance to the opposite party No.2 from the date of filing of an application to the date of judgment and Rs.8000/- per month from the date of impugned judgment.
6. Learned counsel for the revisionist has submitted that trial Court has failed to examine all the documents and illegally passed the impugned order against the revisionist.
He next submitted that opposite party No.2 had left her matrimonial home without any sufficient cause and on her free will and choice, she living separately.
She had filed maintenance petition with wrong facts and baseless allegations.

7. Learned counsel for the revisionist has submitted that opposite party No.2 and her father have given false assertion before the trial Court that the revisionist works in the ICICI Bank as a cashier and they have given contradictory statement also in this regard.

The opposite party No.2 (P.W.1) has stated, in her evidence, that revisionist works in ICICI Bank Delhi whereas (father of the opposite party No.2) P.W.2, has stated in his evidence that revisionist works in Bank of Baroda, Salempur Branch, District Bulandshahar.

8. Learned counsel for the revisionist has submitted that revisionist derives his earning from agricultural activities and he has also filed income certificate issued from Tehsildar, in which,
monthly income of the revisionist has been shown Rs.4000/- per month.

He also filed affidavit in compliance of judgement of the Hon,ble Supreme Court in Rajnish vs. Neha and others passed in Criminal Appeal No. 730 of 2020 (Arising out of SLP (Crl.) No. 9503 of 2018) before the trial Court on 24.04.2024, wherein he has stated that he has 1/5 share in 1.096 hector land, which is agricultural land.
The revisionist has received eduction up to intermediate only and no question arisen that he works in Bank.

He further submitted that trial Court has saddle the revisionist with liability of payment of heavy maintenance his wife without estimating his own income, therefore,
impugned judgment and order is liable to the set aside.
9.

Per contra, learned counsel for the opposite party No.2 has submitted that trial Court has framed four points of determination on the basis of pleadings of the parties and has decided all the points in favour of the revisionist after due appreciation of evidence and findings recorded by the trial Court Gaurav Sharma @ Indramohan vs State Of U.P. 10. The revisionist has filed a copy of an ex-parte judgement and order dated 22.08.2024 passed by the Additional Principle Judge, Family Court, Bulandshahar in Matrimonial Case No.141 of 2020,
whereby decree of restitution of conjugal rights has been passed on application of the revisionist against his wife (opposite party No.2) with a view to impress that opposite party No.2, is not willing to unite with the revisionist, even after decree of restitution of conjugal rights passed by competent Court.

sentences.text:
11. The Hon'ble Supreme Court in Criminal Appeal No.5896 of 2024 (Rina Kumari @ Rina Devi @
Reena) vs. Dinesh Kumar Mahto @ Dinesh Kumat Mahto and another (decided on 10.01.2025) has held that contentions urged on behalf of the revisionist (husband) is that the findings in the judgment for restitution of conjugal rights by the Family Court, being a Civil Court, would be binding on the Court seized of the petition under Section 125 Cr.P.C, as they are to be treated as criminal proceedings.

entities.text:
Criminal Appeal No.5896 of 2024 (Rina Kumari @ Rina Devi @
Reena) vs. Dinesh Kumar Mahto @ Dinesh Kumat Mahto and another
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: This specious argument needs mention only to be rejected outright.

The maintenance proceedings are essentially civil in nature and the reason for inclusion of the provisions dealing therewith in the Code of Criminal Procedure, same was clarified by the Law Commission of India in September, 1969.

This Court in Mst. Jagir Kaur and another vs. Jaswant Singh; AIR 1963 SC 152121 in (3-Judge Bench) held that proceedings under Section 488 of the Code of Criminal Procedure, 1898, the precursor to Section 125 Cr.P.C., are in the nature of civil proceedings; the remedy, being a summary one; and the person seeking that remedy, ordinarily being a helpless person.

entities.text: Mst. Jagir Kaur and another vs. Jaswant Singh; AIR 1963 SC 152121
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Therefore, even if non-compliance with an order for payment of maintenance entails penal consequences, as may other decrees of a Civil Court, such proceedings would not qualify as or become criminal proceedings.
Nomenclature of maintenance proceedings initiated under the Code of Criminal Procedure, as those provisions find place wherein, cannot be held to be conclusive as to the nature of such proceedings.

12. Therefore, in light of the above factum of the Hon'ble Supreme Court, the exparte decree of restitution of conjugal rights passed against the opposite party no.2 in matrimonial proceedings, in which, she did not participate.
It cannot be inferred that she is living separately from her husband neither sufficient cause.
The findings of trial Court are based on evidence on record and need not be interfered.
However, submissions of learned counsel for the revisionist is that trial Court has quantified the amount of maintenance without estimating the monthly earning of the revisionist has got some force.

13. The Hon'ble Supreme Court in Rajnesh vs. Neha and Ors ;Criminal Appeal No. 730 of 2020 (Arising out of SLP (Crl.) No. 9503 of 2018) has held that there is no straitjacket formula for fixing the quantum of maintenance.

sentences.text: Court will take into consideration the family background and other attending circumstances to estimate his actual income.

The contention on behalf of the revisionist is that monthly earnings of the revisionist is reflected in income certificate issued by Tehsildar is not acceptable, as it is a matter of common knowledge that people used to get income certificate from the Revenue Authority by showing their income in lower side with a view to obtain benefit of certain welfare scheme of the Government.
However, quantum of future maintenance, which has been fixed as Rs.8000/- per month appears somewhat excessive and it deserves to be reduced.
As this fact is not proved that the revisionist works as cashier in some bank.

15. Keeping in view the economic status of revisionist, the quantum of maintenance awarded to the revisionist from the date of filing of application to the date of judgment, which is fixed as Rs.4000/-
per month is affirmed.
However, future maintenance fixed as Rs.8000/- per month from the date of judgment dated 23.08.2024 is reduced from Rs.8000/- to Rs.5000/- per month.
Other terms and conditions imposed in the impugned judgment and order are not interfered with and it will be applicable mutantis mutandis, as modified by this judgment and order.
16. The revision is partly allowed accordingly.
